meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'смысленный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('meaningless').

examples.text: Когда второй половинки нет рядом, жизнь бессмысленна.
examples.trans: When our other half is not nearby, life is meaningless.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень бессмысленный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very meaningless choice.

meanings.note: Comparative: ближе. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('close, near').

examples.trans: We have grown closer.
This is my close friend.

examples.text: Слушайте, Марина, мы с вами стали ближе!
examples.trans: Listen, Marina, the two of us have grown closer!

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's always like that.
There's always a way out.
She's offended. She's always like that.

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: Ordinal number. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second').

examples.trans: This is my second term.
The second lesson is hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up
Core Russian part meaning 'let's; come on' in everyday speech.
Casual goodbye. Core Russian part meaning 'let's; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Let's clean up!
See you, bye!
Arkasha, let's clean up!

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.trans: Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, trifle, nothing' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, trifle, nothing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it.
Don't talk nonsense.

examples.text: Да ерунда, мне даже нравится. Как тебе твой новый кандидат?
examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it. How do you like your new candidate?

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's life.
I want a different life.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.trans: The town hall called me.
He's from Moscow.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.trans: I'm looking for a job.
What are you looking for?

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

Кажется as a parenthetical word. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think he's right.
I think I've seen you.
I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Спортивный клуб = sports club. Common substantive noun meaning 'club' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты у нас в клубе танцевала!
examples.trans: You used to dance at our club!
In the evening we are going to a club.

examples.text: Стой, я тебя узнал! Ты у нас в клубе танцевала!
examples.trans: Wait, I recognise you! You used to dance at our club!

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When?
When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'победимый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('invincible').

examples.text: В сердце клуб всегда один, он непобедим.
examples.trans: In the heart there is always one club, it is invincible.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень непобедимый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very invincible choice.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Grab him!

Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Поздравляю! = congratulations!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to congratulate', paired with 'поздравить'.

examples.trans: Great, congratulations!
Happy holiday to you!
Great, congratulations.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ловинка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'other half / partner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Когда второй половинки нет рядом, жизнь бессмысленна.
examples.trans: When our other half is not nearby, life is meaningless.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть половинка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always other half.

meanings.note: + в + prepositional. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to confess, to admit', paired with 'признаваться'.

examples.trans: Well, did he confess?
He confessed to everything.

examples.text: Никак, я тебя на понт взяла. А ты сейчас сама призналась.
examples.trans: No way at all, I called your bluff. And you just confessed yourself.

meanings.note: 'один раз' = once, 'два раза' = twice

examples.trans: Just once.
Say it once more.
What do you mean, once?

meanings.note: Adverb. Core Russian adv meaning 'nearby, next to' in everyday speech.
Рядом с + instrumental. Core Russian adv meaning 'nearby, next to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

examples.text: Теперь меня рядом с ним похоронить не хотят!
examples.trans: Now they won't even bury me next to him!

examples.text: Тут рядом, за углом, чебуречная. Там нормально.
examples.trans: Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café. It's fine there.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: у меня сердце = I have a bad heart (colloquial)

examples.trans: My heart hurts.
He has a kind heart.

examples.text: Мне горько, мне плохо. У меня сердце.
examples.trans: I feel bitter, I feel awful. I have a bad heart.

meanings.en: strong, powerful (also used as a noun: the strong)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strong, powerful').

examples.text: Сильный ищет способ, а слабый ищет причину.
examples.trans: The strong man looks for a way, and the weak man looks for an excuse.
A strong wind was blowing outside.

examples.text: Надо заманить его на свою территорию. Там, где ты сильный.
examples.trans: You need to lure him onto your territory. Right where you are strong.

meanings.note: 3rd-declension feminine noun in -ь. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лабость'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'weakness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You're taking advantage of my weakness!
Everyone has their weaknesses.

examples.text: Ты просто воспользовался моей минутной слабостью.
examples.trans: You simply took advantage of my momentary weakness.

собраться.gloss: to get ready, plan to, gather

meanings.en: to intend, plan, get ready to
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get ready, plan to, gather', paired with 'собираться'.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get ready, plan to, gather', paired with 'собираться'.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?
examples.trans: Are you planning to leave me or what?
We got ready for vacation.
Are you planning to drink alcohol?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'остоять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'consist of'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и состоять вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and consist of on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют состоять.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to consist of.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'петь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sing', paired with 'петь'.

examples.trans: We will sing a song.
We will sing the Bremen musicians' song.

examples.text: Послезавтра вы споёте песню на празднике.
examples.trans: The day after tomorrow you will sing a song at the festival.

meanings.note: Causing fear or feeling frightened. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трашно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I got scared.
Did you really suddenly get scared?

examples.text: Он ночью страшно и громко храпит!
examples.trans: At night he snores terribly and loudly!

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: + acc; зря тратить время = to waste time in vain

examples.trans: Aren't you wasting your time in vain?
Don't spend money on nonsense.

examples.text: А вы сегодня закатали яму во дворе. Вы не зря тратите время?
examples.trans: And today you paved a pothole in a courtyard. Aren't you wasting your time in vain?

meanings.note: Used of either a man or a woman. Common feminine noun meaning 'rag, cloth; (fig.) pushover, wimp' in everyday Russian.
Used of either a man or a woman. Common feminine noun meaning 'rag, cloth; (fig.) pushover, wimp' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если он тряпка, то я нет.
examples.trans: If he's a pushover, I'm not.
Take a clean cloth.

examples.text: Послушай ты, очкарик! Если он тряпка, то я нет.
examples.trans: Listen here, four-eyes! If he's a pushover, I'm not.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

meanings.note: нужно хотя бы поговорить = we need at least to talk
Core Russian part meaning 'even if, at least (with бы); although' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.
Have at least some tea.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.
